items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the social services law, in relation to automated
identification of OTDA assistance program participants
items.lawCode: Amd §131-ss, Soc Serv L (as proposed in S.4548 & A.4876)
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8022

SPONSOR: PARKER
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the social services law, in relation to automated iden-
tification of OTDA assistance program participants

 
PURPOSE:

This is a chapter amendment that makes changes to provisions of L.2023,
c.764, to clarify provisions related to the automated identification
assistance program.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

This legislation amends the underlying chapter by changing the title to
conform with changes made in the definition of automated identification
OTDA assistance program and throughout the legislation, which stem from
the removal of the term "affordability".

Subsection 1(b) adds in a definition for "office or OTDA".

Subsection 1(c) amends the underlying chapter by 1) changing the defi-
nition of "automated identification OTDA assistance program partic-
ipants", 2) providing that the Office of Temporary and Disability
Assistance with the discretion to require written consent from OTDA
assistance program participant's before using data obtained from quali-
fying programs, and 3) limiting the number of qualifying affordability
programs, which may be included in the automated identification assist-
ance program. Under this legislation, qualifying programs include public
assistance, home energy assistance program and any other income-based
assistance program identified by the Public Service Commission and is
administered and approved for inclusion by the office of temporary and
disability assistance.

Subsection 1(d) amends the definition of a "utility corporation" to
include utility companies, utility corporations, public utility compa-
nies, public utility corporations, gas corporations, electric corpo-
rations, or municipalities, a Municipal Corporation that provides public
utility services, a rural electric cooperative, or state public authori-
ty that provides utility services.

Subsection 1(e) amends the definition of "utility corporation energy
affordability programs". These programs must be defined by the Public
Service Commission and must be limited to utility corporation programs
that are intended to assist customers with energy affordability by
reducing customers' energy burden.

Subsection 2 amends the underlying chapter by changing the timeline, in
which OTDA's commissioner must provide for the automated identification
of OTDA assistance program participants for participation in utility
corporation energy affordability programs, from 180 days to a year of
the effective date of the legislation.

Subsection 3 amends the underlying chapter by requiring utility corpo-
rations be responsible for working with OTDA to facilitate and implement
the technological capabilities to allow for the secure transmission of

data through an interface with OTDA's information technology infrastruc-
ture.

Subsection 4(a) amends the underlying chapter by adding that the OTDA,
as long as permitted by federal law, regulation and policy, where a
utility corporation agrees and signs OTDA's data terms and OTDA has
receipt of such corporation's data terms, must conduct an automated file
matching to identify utility corporation customer accounts that are also
OTDA assistance program participants and must provide such information
to utility corporations at least twice a year. This subsection also
provides that any utility corporation customers that are identified as
potentially eligible, by OTDA's data match, and are confirmed to be
eligible for the utility corporation's energy affordability programs, by
the utility corporation, must be enrolled in the utility corporation
energy affordability program within 60 days after the utility corpo-
ration was provided receipt of the automated file match.

Subsection 4(b) amends the underlying chapter by adding that any infor-
mation provided to utility corporations that relates to the OTDA assist-
ance program participants must not be re-disclosed by the utility corpo-
ration and must only be utilized for the purposes of confirming
eligibility in the utility corporation's energy affordability program
and to provide required written notification to utility corporation
energy affordability program participants of their enrollment in the
program.

Subsection 4(c) amends the underlying chapter by adding language, which
provides, unless prohibited by federal law, regulation, or policy, a
utility corporation, notwithstanding any provision of state or local
law, regulation, or policy to the contrary, is authorized to share the
required data elements as it pertains to this legislation.

Lastly, this legislation amends the underlying chapter by adding that
the Commissioner of OTDA may delegate the administration of any portion
of this section to any state agency, social services official, city,
county, town contractor or nonprofit organization; and if delegated,
privacy and confidentiality limitations that are set out in this section
will apply to said entity.

 
EXISTING LAW:

None.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This legislation is a negotiated change to the underlying chapter.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

Chapter amendment to Chapter 764 of the Laws of 2023 5.4548 and A.4876
passed the Senate and Assembly, respectfully, in June 2023.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the same date and in the same manner as a
chapter of the laws of 2023 relating to providing for the automated
identification of affordability program participants, as proposed in
legislative bills numbers S.4548 and A.4876, takes effect.

summary: Relates to automated identification of OTDA assistance program participants; identifies entities to be defined as a "utility corporation"; requires utility corporations to administer secure transmission of participant data; requires utility corporations to conduct automated file matching with OTDA assistance program participant accounts; directs utility corporations to notify participants of automatic enrollment in utility corporation affordability program; makes related provisions.
title: Relates to automated identification of OTDA assistance program participants
